successCriteria.description: The Employee entity type is exported from the employee module and declares exactly the canonical fields with their canonical types from the reconciled architecture: id (string), employeeNumber (string), firstName (string), lastName (string), email (string), managerId (string|null), department (string|null), hireDate (Date), terminationDate (Date|null), employmentStatus ('ACTIVE'|'INACTIVE'|'TERMINATED'), createdAt (Date), updatedAt (Date), deletedAt (Date|null). employmentStatus is a string-literal union, not a runtime enum.

The IEmployeeRepository interface declares all eight operations from the phase scope: findById(id), findByEmployeeNumber(employeeNumber), findByManagerId(managerId), findByDepartment(department), findActive(), save(employee), update(id, partial), softDelete(id). A concrete PgEmployeeRepository class implements IEmployeeRepository and is exported from the module's public entry point.

The repository persists and retrieves Employee rows against the employees table, mapping snake_case DB columns (employee_number, first_name, last_name, manager_id, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) to/from the camelCase domain model fields. A row round-tripped through save then findById returns an Employee whose domain fields equal the input.

All read operations (findById, findByEmployeeNumber, findByManagerId, findByDepartment, findActive) exclude soft-deleted rows — rows where deleted_at IS NOT NULL are never returned. softDelete(id) sets deleted_at (and does not physically delete the row), after which findById(id) returns null/undefined for that id.

findActive() returns only employees whose employmentStatus is 'ACTIVE' (and are not soft-deleted). findByEmployeeNumber returns the unique employee matching that employee number (or null when none), respecting the unique index on employee_number.

save(employee) inserts a new employee row and returns the persisted Employee; update(id, partial) applies only the supplied fields and returns the updated Employee (updatedAt is refreshed). softDelete(id) is idempotent — calling it on an already-deleted id does not error.

Jest unit tests exist under tests/unit/modules/employee/ covering both the Employee model (field/type shape) and every IEmployeeRepository method (with the pg Pool mocked), and the full test suite passes via the project's configured test command.

The employee module's public entry point (index.ts) re-exports the Employee type, the IEmployeeRepository interface, and the PgEmployeeRepository class, so downstream phases (LeaveBalance, LeaveRequest, Employee service) can import them through the module boundary only.
